purpose: Separate the commands and files future users can treat as RedCap's public runtime contract from maintainer-only governance, release-readiness, and source-repository support tools.
public_contract_summary: The end-user runtime contract is the small CLI surface needed to revive a workspace, inspect status, run safe diagnostics, collect debug context, and close out a task.
alpha_readiness_boundary: The package candidate may still include maintainer/readiness validators while RedCap remains private=true and publish_allowed=false. Those files are packaged only to support source-repo readiness checks and must not be presented as stable end-user API.

public_api_must_not_depend_on: compass/tools/* checker names as user-facing API
Norven-local identity, reports, prompt scratch files, or credentials
full source-governance validators as normal end-user workflow
release_task_must_redecide: whether maintainer/readiness tools remain in the public npm tarball
whether a separate maintainer profile or package is needed
license, registry credentials, publish_allowed=true, and npm publish

package_candidate_classes.description: Thin CLI facade, root compatibility facades, and package-visible runtime wrappers.
Package-visible host adapter documentation and compatibility layer.
Human-readable product, architecture, handoff, dictionary, and public template documentation.
Scripts needed by revive/status/diagnose/closeout and alpha readiness checks. They may be packaged for operation but are not stable direct user API.
Prism availability, dispatch, evidence and lifecycle helpers packaged as support tooling, not as the core end-user runtime API.
Machine-readable policies that explain and validate the package/readiness boundary.
